evidence.reason: Lines 141-150 show the `sourcePr`↔`job.pr` binding being validated inside `canonical()`, but line 150 returns `null` immediately when a job has no current fixed event, skipping validation of every subsequent job in `input.jobs`. The unconditional pre-loop at 112-124 checks `same(fresh, entry.job)`, item, run and path anchors but does NOT check the `sourcePr`↔`pr` binding, so that binding is only enforced inside the short-circuiting loop. A later job whose recorded `pr` disagrees with its `sourcePr` is therefore never rejected when an earlier job lacks a fixed event; the fallback path (per the finding, Feedback posted to `sourcePr` at line 241) can then act on the unvalidated binding. This is an ordering/validation error in existing intended behavior, not a new requirement; the minimal fix is to validate all job identities and `sourcePr` bindings in a first pass, then collect terminal events and return `null` only after those checks complete. Routine correctness repair, no owner decision needed.
